title: Understanding Pointers in C
summary: Learn how pointers store memory addresses and manipulate data indirectly.

scenes.narration: Welcome to learning about pointers in C!
scenes.heading: Understanding Pointers in C

scenes.narration: We start with our main function and declare an integer variable x initialized with the value 10.
Next, we declare a pointer variable ptr and assign it the address of x using the ampersand operator.
We print the value of x using the format specifier %d for integers.
Now, we print the address of x using the format specifier %p for pointers.
Finally, we print the value at the address stored in ptr using the dereference operator asterisk.
The output shows the value of x, then its address, which is different every time you run it, then the value at ptr, which is the same 10 as x.
scenes.output:
Value of x: 10
Address of x: 0x7ffd5e8c3a4c
Value at ptr: 10

scenes.narration: In summary, pointers are variables that hold memory addresses, allowing us to access and manipulate data indirectly.
points: Use the ampersand operator to get an address.
Use the asterisk operator to access the value at an address.
